Design effect of a share with sources as clusters

Source: R/share_intervals.R
cluster_deff.Rd

Treats the share of a code as a ratio estimator x / n summed over clusters (sources) and computes its linearised between-cluster variance, the design effect with respect to the binomial variance, the intra-cluster correlation and the effective number of clusters.

Usage

cluster_deff(
  counts,
  key_cols,
  cluster_col = "source",
  x_col = "x",
  n_col = "n",
  cluster_totals = NULL
)

Arguments

counts

data.frame or data.table with one row per key and cluster, holding the count x_col and (when cluster_totals is NULL) the cluster denominator n_col.

key_cols

Character vector of key columns (e.g. the code).

cluster_col

Name of the cluster column (default "source").

x_col

Name of the count column (default "x").

n_col

Name of the denominator column (default "n"), in counts or in cluster_totals.

cluster_totals

Optional data.frame with one row per cluster and columns cluster_col and n_col. When given, the denominator of every cluster is taken from it and every cluster with a positive denominator enters the variance of every key, also when the key has no row (zero count) for that cluster. Recommended.

Value

A data.table with one row per key and columns key_cols, x, n, quota, v_bin, v_cluster, deff, rho, n_cluster, n_cluster_eff, df.

Details

For a key with cluster counts x_s and denominators n_s (s = 1, ..., S, clusters with n_s > 0), x = sum(x_s), n = sum(n_s) and p = x / n. The linearised (Taylor) variance of the ratio estimator with clusters as primary units (Wolter, 2007) is

v_cluster = S / (S - 1) * sum_s (x_s - p n_s)^2 / n^2

and the binomial variance is v_bin = p (1 - p) / n. The design effect (Kish, 1965) is deff = v_cluster / v_bin (NA when p is 0 or 1, or when S < 2). With the weighted mean cluster size m = sum(n_s^2) / n, the intra-cluster correlation implied by deff = 1 + (m - 1) rho is rho = (deff - 1) / (m - 1). The effective number of clusters is n_cluster_eff = n^2 / sum(n_s^2) and df = n_cluster_eff - 1 is the suggested number of degrees of freedom for share_interval().

Clusters with a zero count for the key contribute (p n_s)^2 to the sum. Without cluster_totals only the rows present in counts enter the computation, so counts must then be complete (one row per key and cluster, zeros included).

References

Kish, L. (1965). Survey Sampling. Wiley.

Wolter, K. M. (2007). Introduction to Variance Estimation (2nd ed.). Springer.

Examples

counts <- data.frame(
  code = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 4),
  source = rep(c("s1", "s2", "s3", "s4"), 2),
  x = c(10, 40, 5, 25, 3, 2, 4, 1)
)
totals <- data.frame(source = c("s1", "s2", "s3", "s4"),
                     n = c(200, 400, 100, 300))
cluster_deff(counts, key_cols = "code", cluster_totals = totals)
#>      code     x     n quota    v_bin    v_cluster     deff         rho
#>    <char> <num> <num> <num>    <num>        <num>    <num>       <num>
#> 1:      a    80  1000  0.08 7.36e-05 0.0001466667 1.992754 0.003320246
#> 2:      b    10  1000  0.01 9.90e-06 0.0000240000 2.424242 0.004763353
#>    n_cluster n_cluster_eff       df
#>        <int>         <num>    <num>
#> 1:         4      3.333333 2.333333
#> 2:         4      3.333333 2.333333
